semantics.transitionSystem: Each feature is modeled as a partial transition F : I x S -> O x S'. requires defines the admissible input domain; ensures defines the post-state; invariants hold for every reachable transition; failures defines the conservative result outside the domain.
semantics.quantification: Unless a clause says bounded, variables are universally quantified over the stated admissible domain.
semantics.verificationMeaning: bounded-exhaustive and property evidence checks finite models; integration and regression evidence are executable refinement witnesses; static evidence checks types/build/configuration. Network and deployment contracts are not claimed as theorem-proved.

globalInvariants.statement: Every number used for price, quantity, exposure, probability, score, cost, or time arithmetic is finite and in its declared range before it can change money or persistent state.
Malformed, missing, stale, unauthenticated, or contradictory evidence cannot create or increase exposure, privilege, freshness, confidence, or deployment authority.
A decision at event time t depends only on evidence whose publication/event time is <= t; targets and later outcomes are excluded.
A reduce-only transition cannot increase absolute exposure, change its sign without passing through zero, or create exposure from flat.
Executed quantity, equity, fees, and cost buckets reconcile at every state transition within the declared floating-point tolerance.
Credentials, state, jobs, cache entries, bot workers, and operations are isolated by one unambiguous tenant identity.
Retryable create/update/import/publish operations have a stable identity and repeated application cannot duplicate their durable effect.
Secrets never appear in committed files, URLs, public runtime configuration, telemetry, exception text, or ordinary logs.
Queues, retries, buffers, requests, histories, process lifetimes, and search spaces have explicit non-negative finite bounds.
For fixed validated inputs, seed, configuration, and prior state, pure computation and serialized ordering are deterministic.
A deployment or branch promotion identifies an exact source revision and occurs only after the canonical checks for every changed surface pass.
Training, calibration, optimization, validation, and reported historical performance preserve chronological splits and embargoes and never fit preprocessing on future rows.

Before creating report output, the exporter reconciles unique supplied roster IDs, start/terminal lifecycle (only failed-fit cascades may omit starts), training/replay identities and seed/fold metadata, statuses/reasons/observation counts, successful-fit artifact digests, OPE fit coverage, total/group counts and descriptive return/risk/cost aggregates. Evaluated RL rows require finite nonnegative latency p99 and OOD rates in [0,1], using the same family classification as reporting. Peak-memory metadata must be finite and nonnegative. All compact reports are rendered before output creation and written as UTF-8 bytes with explicit LF terminators, so field and serialization errors cannot leave partial reports or trigger platform newline translation; filesystem write failures are not atomic. Contradictory, missing, duplicated or malformed evidence in these fields is rejected.

Replay indices and horizons, collection seeds and transition budgets require Python or NumPy integers excluding booleans, with existing episode bounds, horizons 1/3/6, nonnegative seeds and positive budgets. Replay market inputs are aligned real unmasked one-dimensional arrays. Collection requires matching nonempty string-symbol maps and at least 121 aligned training bars per symbol; admission precedes RNG sampling. Execution coefficients are finite real nonboolean scalars in their existing ranges, and behavior probabilities require real unmasked vectors. Admission inspects representation and bounds only; trailing feature values and actual transition scalars are validated when consumed, without scanning unused future values.

Collection admits a learning transition only after finite reward/equity and causal time progress are checked. Nonterminal samples require a real unmasked finite 12-component successor and the complete decision interval. Terminal samples require absent successor, zero inventory, no pending target and a normal episode endpoint or an accounted capital-floor, drawdown, exposure or turnover stop. Invalid-market, invalid-observation, permission and insolvency failures abort collection instead of becoming zero-reward terminals or fabricated successor vectors; the call returns no partial batch. Fully accounted risk losses remain training samples.

Scale construction snapshots six-component real unmasked parameter vectors onto immutable float64 backing bytes, rejects non-finite values, nonpositive deviations and inverted support bounds, and cannot alias mutable caller arrays. Fitting requires nonempty list/tuple prefixes with at least 25 real unmasked prices each and never silently drops short supplied prefixes. Transform and support queries require finite real unmasked six-component vectors; unsupported input returns false and invalid or overflowing normalization raises instead of returning a directional/non-finite value. Replay converts normalization ValueError into an absent observation before new fills. Existing valid fitted float64 semantics and JSON provenance fields are unchanged.

Policy save and load share a v1 parameter contract with exact w1/b1/w2/b2 names and shapes 12x16/16/16x3/3. Writers snapshot real unmasked numeric arrays and reject malformed fields, booleans, object/complex arrays, wrong shapes and non-finite portable values before opening the output file. Readers reject nonnumeric JSON leaves before applying the same shape/finite-value contract. Floating parameters use portable float64 while integer JSON values retain their representation. Valid writes remain bounded to 65536 bytes and exclusive; an invalid save returns no success digest, and runner failure accounting retains every planned trial without a successful-fit artifact. Filesystem write failures are not an atomic-write guarantee.

PPO and Q training validate integer horizons, seeds and positive step budgets before model construction or RNG use. Python/NumPy integers excluding booleans are admitted only for horizons 1/3/6, nonnegative seeds and positive budgets, then converted to Python integers before seed offsets or batch arithmetic. Q training requires an exact Python boolean offline mode and validates execution/risk coefficients before initialization. Zero/negative budgets cannot return an untrained PPO policy as a successful fit, truthy nonboolean modes cannot select an algorithm, and fixed-width arithmetic cannot wrap training controls. Registered parameters and valid learning behavior remain unchanged; this is not a compute-budget ceiling.

Collection records every admitted terminal episode immediately, including the final requested decision and accounted risk stops. Optional episodeAccountingV2 metadata counts collections, started/completed/truncated episodes and decisions; completion denotes terminal accounting, not successful performance. Budget-truncated episodes retain nonterminal successors without invented liquidation or episode returns. Trainers sum counts across actual collections. Before export, v2 counts must be nonnegative integers excluding booleans, match the algorithm's collection schedule, positive step budget and terminal records, and reconcile started = completed + truncated. Unknown accounting versions and invalid terminal outcomes fail before report output. Legacy records without v2 retain their original bytes and unknown coverage; no historical report is rewritten or promoted.

Terminal ledger publication and replay return-path writes occur outside computational exception handlers. A write, flush or serialization error at those boundaries aborts the runner before final summary/index publication, without appending a replacement model-failure outcome or retrying an uncertain terminal. Partial files and possibly flushed terminal lines remain incomplete evidence and are not automatically resumed. Genuine training/artifact-admission, OPE and replay-computation exceptions retain existing failed-trial accounting. Successful archive semantics are unchanged. This does not provide atomic filesystem publication, fsync durability or crash recovery.

The exporter decodes the admitted evidence-index bytes, all seven verified report-input snapshots and each JSONL event with one JSON admission contract. Duplicate object keys at any depth, including identical values and escaped-key collisions, are rejected before a value is discarded. NaN/Infinity constants and floating-point literals that overflow to non-finite values are rejected even in fields omitted by report rendering. Decoding never reopens verified report paths; failures precede output-directory creation. Valid finite JSON values, integer semantics and legacy report bytes remain unchanged. This is a decoding boundary, not a canonical-encoding requirement, authenticity proof, schema-completeness claim or bounded-memory guarantee.

Evidence export resolves source and output paths once at admission and uses those resolved paths throughout. A destination equal to or beneath the admitted source archive is rejected before reading evidence or creating directories, including symlink aliases and dot-dot spellings. Retargeting the original destination alias after admission cannot redirect report publication into the source. Valid external destinations retain exclusive directory creation, exact report bytes and archive file inventory/content. Existing external outputs are not overwritten. This assumes resolved directory ancestors remain stable and does not provide inode locking, mount-alias detection or atomic multi-file publication.

Before compact report publication, any supplied training duration in a fit or its terminal event must be a finite nonnegative real JSON number, excluding booleans; if both supply durations they must agree exactly. Supplied artifact byte counts must be positive JSON integers, excluding booleans. Missing legacy fields remain optional. Export admits only explicit bytes or kib RSS units before evidence reads. Valid measurements and legacy report bytes retain their semantics. This validates metadata domains and cross-record agreement, not measurement accuracy, completeness or artifact byte-count identity.

Offline baseline action and forecast entry points admit only recognized names and unmasked, one-dimensional, 12-element finite real NumPy observations, excluding boolean, complex and object representations. Invalid observations or unknown names return absence before rule computation or random sampling. Forecast names are limited to the five implemented forecasting rules. A rejected action remains absent, not a request to flatten, and replay shielding rejects it without a fill. Valid baseline outputs and RNG semantics are preserved. This is input admission, not fitted-parameter validation, a timeout guarantee or a complete simulator/OPE audit.

OPE admission rejects NumPy masked arrays in rewards, logged actions, behavior probabilities, target probabilities, Q estimates and V estimates before array coercion can discard the mask. Partial, full and all-false masks are rejected without imputation, row deletion or caller mutation. Ordinary supported unmasked arrays and array-like inputs retain existing estimates. The runner records rejection as an explicit failed OPE outcome while retaining the completed fit; compact reports preserve the failure and remain non-authorizing. This does not establish behavior support, estimator reliability or market generalization.

Offline baselines validate the fitted scalar/vector/matrix parameters used by each selected rule: finite real values, exact coefficient shapes, no boolean/object/complex/masked representations, and an allowed behavior-clone action. Forecast/action arithmetic rejects overflow and non-finite intermediate values before logistic clipping, argmax or utility selection. Failed computations return absence; replay shielding rejects absence without a fill. Valid formulas, tie-breaking, finite-logit clipping and RNG behavior remain unchanged; unrelated invalid fitted components do not disable independent constant/uniform rules. This does not establish parameter provenance, calibration, timeout guarantees or economic value.

Short OPE replay validates every observation passed to the policy and every resulting value vector before selection or transition on both logged-behavior and direct-policy paths. Inputs must be finite real unmasked 12-element NumPy vectors; outputs must be finite real unmasked three-element NumPy vectors. Malformed observations fail before forward inference; malformed outputs fail before the affected transition. Failures remain explicit and do not become cash actions, clipped values or excluded episodes. Valid policy action traces, tie-breaking, RNG and unsupported-state behavior remain unchanged. This does not calibrate policy values, guarantee inference time or establish OPE reliability.

Short OPE admits its whole request before RNG construction or policy calls. Horizon/start/stop/seed/episode budget are genuine Python or NumPy integers, excluding booleans; they normalize to Python integers before arithmetic. Horizons are 1/3/6, seed is nonnegative, budget positive, and 24 <= start < stop - 6*horizon. Price/funding dictionaries have identical nonempty string symbol sets and aligned one-dimensional real unmasked arrays covering the complete exclusive stop bound. Admission inspects representation/length only; future values are consumed causally by replay. Valid RNG, policy, failed-episode and result semantics are preserved. This does not authenticate data, register a budget or establish OPE reliability.

Economic reporting requires an explicitly stopped replay and, when present, a nonblank string failure reason distinct from complete. Successful completion requires the final outcome bar, finite zero inventory, no pending action, finite positive equity equal to the final row, and the full expected bar count. Unfinished or inconsistent successful paths fail before metric computation. Explicitly failed stopped paths retain their failure identity and recorded losses, including zero-row and unliquidated partial paths. Valid completed report bytes are preserved. This checks completion state, not every ledger field or the recoverability/liquidation value of failed inventory.

Economic reporting admits contiguous recorded bars from start+1 through the stopped replay index, finite real metric inputs excluding booleans, and nonnegative turnover and cost buckets. Each equity transition reconciles prior equity plus gross P&L and funding less costs within relative/absolute tolerance 1e-10; each net return reconciles equity/prior equity minus one within 1e-12. Prior equity is positive; a finite nonpositive final equity remains reportable for an explicitly failed path. Final recorded equity equals replay equity. Invalid evidence raises before metric computation; valid report bytes and failed-path losses are preserved. This is internal ledger consistency, not fill reconstruction, market-data authenticity, action-counter validation or economic confirmation.

Offline neural forward evaluation rejects floating-point overflow and invalid arithmetic and requires finite hidden preactivations before tanh and finite outputs before returning values. The contract covers actor and critic vector/batch evaluation; finite saturation remains valid. Inference catches failure as an absent proposal, which shielding rejects without a fill; OPE failure occurs before the affected transition. Valid forward bytes, action semantics and persistence format remain unchanged. This does not certify parameter provenance, validate all representations or gradients/optimizer state, guarantee a preemptive timeout or establish economic value.

Offline Adam updates require a positive finite real learning rate and a nonnegative integer step counter, excluding booleans. Non-finite gradients, overflowing clipping norms and invalid Adam arithmetic fail explicitly. Candidate parameters and moments are computed without mutating current state and published with the incremented counter only after every candidate array is finite. Under non-mutating helpers and a single writer, a failure before publication leaves parameters, both moments and counter unchanged; this does not repair pre-existing corruption. Final attribute stores are sequential and require uninterrupted successful completion; interruption or concurrent observation is not atomic (CE-RL-016). Stronger atomicity remains an unresolved acceptance obligation. Valid update formulas and numerical results remain compatible. This does not certify every input representation, hidden gradient intermediate, state shape, convergence or economic value and grants no order authority.

The offline screen captures its registered source and registration files once before data admission and compares those exact bytes with blobs from one resolved Git commit. It parses the registration and computes source/registration provenance from admitted snapshots, retaining the same registration hash in the manifest and every saved policy. Later pathname replacement cannot change parsed settings or relabel provenance. Mismatching captured bytes reject before dataset access or archive creation; a fresh invocation validates fresh snapshots. Valid artifact fields and hashes retain their semantics. This checks file bytes, not loaded-interpreter attestation, dependency/environment identity, Git trust, data authenticity or economic efficacy; no order authority or promotion permission is added.

ensures.statement: Every simulated policy-target fill occurs after its originating decision. Mandatory terminal liquidation occurs at the current terminal endpoint after old inventory earns that interval's price/funding; entry and liquidation costs both apply if a pending target fills at that endpoint. Fees, spread, slippage, impact sensitivity and terminal liquidation reconcile equity.
All planned algorithms, horizons, seeds, folds and replays remain in the roster; failed/stopped paths are not cash-padded or discarded for promotion statistics.

Run manifests and policy provenance retain the registered hashes proven at snapshot admission. Replacing either input pathname after admission cannot change parsed prices/funding or relabel their provenance; a subsequent invocation rejects unregistered replacement bytes before parsing.

Archive path replacement after successful verification cannot change exported report inputs or the admitted external index identity. Unchanged archived evidence produces byte-identical compact reports. This preserves evidence identity without granting promotion authority or asserting that source paths remain immutable.

Internal archive reconciliation preserves failed fits and stopped replays in descriptive statistics and rejects missing OPE rows or malformed v1 OPE outcome payloads for successful fits. OPE schema checks require nonempty failed/invalid outcomes or complete finite conditional-estimate/support/interval fields with reliability false; they do not establish estimator truth. Nested result fields cannot shadow validated trial identity in exported CSVs. Failed training/terminal/replay outcomes require nonblank non-reserved reasons and complete outcomes have no reason; training-row reasons must match terminal-event reasons. The runner records exception class names in training/OPE/replay failure reasons, including empty or reserved messages, so these failures remain exportable without losing trials. Manifest and summary dispositions must remain non-authorizing contaminated development with no candidate passed, no opened holdout and null v1 promotion statistics before output creation. Original v1 successful training records without a status field remain supported when ledger completion and verified artifact identity agree. Reconciliation does not establish external preregistration completeness, recompute path economics or validate OPE estimates.

invariants.statement: Haskell ResearchProposal has no order identity; its constructor is private and orderAuthorized is always False. This isolated module has no production caller. Deterministic risk evidence takes precedence over every accepted target.

Default mode is Disabled. Python enabled/valid/ownership gates require exact boolean True, not truthiness; timing and actions require finite real scalars excluding booleans, complex values and arrays. Replay rejects invalid gates before reading observations or processing pending fills. Inference accepts finite real unmasked vectors of the declared widths and returns an absent proposal on model exceptions; its elapsed-time gate is post-call, not preemptive. Offline opt-in permits only target values -0.25, 0, 0.25; malformed observation, action, provenance, support, ownership or timeout returns absent/rejected. No live authorization, deployment, production self-modification, automatic checkpoint promotion or production retraining route exists.

Environment, observation, action, reward and policy versions are explicit. PPO evaluation is deterministic. Logged behavior is simulated and cannot be presented as exchange support. No shadow, paper or micro-live readiness is inferred from this screen.

failures.statement: Hash/schema/version/provenance/non-finite failure or timeout rejects an artifact/proposal. Risk breach terminates the path as failed; valid terminal inventory is charged liquidation costs, with no synthetic continuation.
Missing independent data, champion parity, state-action coverage, reliable OPE, statistical tests or realistic fills fails promotion completeness; it is never interpreted as zero risk.

Malformed OPE input or non-finite importance-weight, moment, estimate or bootstrap arithmetic raises an explicit invalid-batch error; weights are never clipped to manufacture support. Zero target support retains ESS zero and absent WIS. A finite estimate never grants promotion authority.

requires.statement: Signed private requests require explicit credentials, canonical parameters, bounded clock skew, venue-valid symbol/filter/quantity, and a live-trading authorization witness.

Availability-aware observations preserve distinct event and availability timestamps with 0 <= eventTime <= availabilityTime <= decisionTime.

Availability-aware alignment preserves per-family value, observed mask, selected event time, and selected availability time; a revision cannot affect a bar that closed before the revision became available.

The external panel decoder is not connected to legacy feature construction or production orchestration, so disabled v2 decoding cannot change an existing model input, prediction, or signal.

Changing or appending a future decoded derivatives row cannot change an already-produced feature prefix.

Changing or appending future external observations cannot alter an existing feature prefix; the external-family adapter remains absent from legacy feature, artifact, predictor, bot, and execution imports.

Empty, reordered, malformed, non-finite, non-canonical, mixed-scope, duplicate-time, out-of-order, or coverage-incoherent v2 panels fail as a whole before feature construction.

Partial, non-finite, non-binary, non-causal, future-available, freshness-incoherent, stale-nonzero, duplicate-header, unordered, or overflowed derivatives v2 evidence fails decoding before it can become a feature.

An optional unavailable value has dense value zero and mask false, an observed zero has mask true, and unavailable required evidence yields no row.

Negative or incoherent timestamps, future availability, missing or non-finite required values, invalid complete-case OHLCV, empty or duplicate fields, ambiguous field names, and structurally misaligned cross-exchange bars fail closed before model input construction.

Derivatives artifact verification recomputes columns, scope, rows, time order, coverage, fresh-tail versioning, refresh lag/count arithmetic, and every present v2 value/mask/timestamp from the causally aligned bound ledgers after validating all file hashes.

failures.statement: Missing tool, uncovered file, stale evidence marker, spec cycle, or failed check returns non-zero.

specifications.title: Fly, AWS, Render, and container deployment

requires.statement: Deployment identifies an already verified commit/image digest, validates required secret references without interpolating plaintext JSON, and declares rollback/health criteria.

ensures.statement: Running service reports the selected commit, exposes only intended ports/routes, uses injected secrets, and reaches health before promotion succeeds.

invariants.statement: Research and trading roles remain isolated; deployment tenant derivation matches backend canonical legacy and v2 vectors; temporary credential material is removed on every exit path; rerun converges idempotently.

failures.statement: Build, secret, migration, health, or promotion failure leaves the last healthy release active and emits no secret.

evidence.contains: AWS tenant derivation matches the canonical legacy and v2 vectors

specifications.title: Hetzner trading/research roles, Caddy, Postgres, webhook bridge, and remote deploy

requires.statement: Trading is live iff effective CLI and environment authorization are both explicitly true; research cannot route private order endpoints; remote tree projects one exact verified commit.

ensures.statement: Compose starts only declared available artifacts, role-specific credentials/routes, local durable Postgres, and health-checked services at the recorded commit.

invariants.statement: TRADER_BINANCE_LIVE=false or TRADER_BOT_TRADE=false implies no real order path; removed tracked files cannot remain active remotely; webhook target exists when configured.

failures.statement: Missing service artifact, contradictory safety toggle, role leak, sync drift, or failed health aborts promotion and leaves trading disabled.

specifications.title: Continuous integration, scheduled jobs, and deployment promotion

requires.statement: Workflow permissions are least privilege, secrets are injected by the platform, concurrency policy is explicit, and deployment consumes a successful verified commit.

ensures.statement: Required checks cover Haskell, web, automation/formal registry and deployment-specific validation before the exact commit is promoted.

invariants.statement: A failed/cancelled/skipped required check cannot be interpreted as green; manual dispatch cannot deploy an unverified branch tip.

failures.statement: Missing secret, failed check, stale commit, or concurrent superseding run prevents promotion.
